top_strength: Clean, confident pricing mechanics on a long-haul quote that would trip up most reps. Chris led with the right opener - "our pricing is super simple" - then built the number transparently in front of the customer: the $111 per mover rate, the two-man team, the one-time $1,056 transportation fee, the 2.5 hour minimum and 15-minute increments, landing on a specific bottom line, "You'd be looking at $2,610." He also sold budget-consciously without being asked, volunteering the weekday and Sunday tiers where "you'd save at least a couple of $100." And when the customer surfaced the one thing that actually worried him, Chris answered it straight: "we move beds, it's a little tricky to get it apart and get it back going but the guys have done them multiple times."
coaching_note: He quoted the price and then let the customer walk. There was no ask - the close was "I'll send an email, if you have any questions, just want to book it, just respond to email or call us back" - and the customer left with "we'll get back to you." This was a ready buyer with a hard deadline (mom has to be out by the 27th) and a date already picked. The single highest-value change: after the number lands, ask for the booking on the call, and lead into it with the two things that make the no-risk ask easy - no deposit, free to cancel or reschedule - instead of burying them mid-paragraph. Second, the differentiators never got said: No Worries $2,000 coverage, Meet Your Mover and the On-Time Guarantee were all absent on a call where an 83-year-old mother's China cabinet and crystal figurines were the emotional center of the job. That was the moment to sell damage coverage, not skip it.
phone_presence_notes: Polite and competent but transactional - he delivered pricing in long uninterrupted blocks that reduced the customer to repeated "Okay"s, never used either name cleanly, and let a real emotional disclosure ("this is my eighty three-year. Old mother... She can't really take care of her so fun anymore") pass with no acknowledgment, though the customer stayed positive and closed with "I sure appreciate that."
